acceptance: A develop CI job or pr-preflight step fails when a test would fail or error on the curated release tree because it reads a stripped path.
The check uses the same curation commands as release-cut, read from one source, so the two cannot drift.
The release guide documents how to fix a failure: strip the test or skip it on the specific file it reads.
A dry run of release curation on current develop passes the CI fast selection, apart from known environment-only failures.
context:
Found during the v0.4.2 release. Release PR #2648 failed test with 12 failures and 31 errors, #2655 with 3 failures and 2 errors, both FileNotFoundError/ModuleNotFoundError on stripped paths. Simulation recipe used: extract the release-cut target's 'git rm' lines from the Makefile, run them in a detached scratch worktree, then run: uv run -- python -m pytest tests -m "fast and not (slow or stress or resource_heavy or live_integration)" -n auto. Related: dlv2-53-retire-legacy-release-path.

Progress 2026-10-06 (owner kept the legacy release path for 0.4.3): PR #2733, branch fix/release-curation-drift-check, worktree ../BenchBox.wt-curation-drift, head f7344693a. Design: scripts/release_curation_dry_run.py reads the git rm commands from the release-cut recipe via check_release_curation.release_cut_rm_commands (the parser check_release_curation.py already used, now shared), applies them in a detached scratch worktree of HEAD, and runs pytest there with test.yml's marker selection. CI: a step in ci.yml's code-test job runs it for the PR's changed test modules (seconds; a full fast run costs ~23 CI minutes). Full run (no arguments) is documented in the release guide's new "Tests on the release tree" section for use before a cut. No Makefile change was needed, which also avoids make/inventory.json churn. Not done: a full dry run in release-canary.yml (its summary schema is read by readiness tooling; possible follow-up). The first full run on develop 70c055227 found 6 real release-tree failures (test_api_reference_contract x2, test_uat_loc_bucket_coverage x3, test_corpus_cohort_depth import error); each now skips when its specific _project file or removed fixture is absent. A second full run left only my new test's marker-policy violation, now fixed. Tests: new test_release_curation_dry_run.py (fails on a newly added test that reads a removed path; passes on shipped paths); test_check_release_curation.py passes; pr-preflight 180 passed. Resume: confirm the third full dry run result (scratchpad log dryrun-full3.log), add it to the PR body, watch to merge (Makefile untouched but ci.yml may need an owner oracle-review stand-in), then finish.
description: The release-cut target removes development-only paths (_project, AGENTS.md, .pre-commit-config.yaml and others) and a hand-maintained list of tests that read them. New tests that read those paths are not added to the list, so the next release PR fails its required test job and blocks release-required-result. v0.4.0, v0.4.1 and v0.4.2 each hit this; v0.4.2 needed two develop fixes (#2651, #2658) and three cuts. A local run of the CI fast selection on a simulated curated tree takes 3-5 minutes and found every remaining failure at once. Add a check on develop that applies the release curation to a scratch tree and runs collection or the fast test selection, or a static check that fails when a test outside the strip list references a stripped path. Prefer skipping individual tests on the specific file they read (the pattern used in #2658) over stripping whole files that mostly test shipped code.
